Account background: Cobalt Helix is a mid-market contact center SaaS provider (omnichannel). Building an agent-assist layer to upsell to enterprise customers. Current stack: proprietary routing + Twilio for telephony; want to replace/augment assistant layer with low-latency streaming suggestions and tool-calling integrations.

Recent timeline / activity:
- 2025-11-12: initial inbound via website, AE outreach (Evan).
- 2026-01-08: discovery call (30m) w/ Product + Eng (Priya joined). Notes: primary ask = real-time streaming suggestions, succinct ticket summaries, and secure tool-calls into internal CRM. "We need something that won't slow down the rep at peak" - Lead PM.
- 2026-02-18: platform demo (Fireflies ff-20260218-CHX-kickoff). Showed Redwood hosted API streaming; customer asked about p99 latency numbers and fallback behavior.

Use-case & technical requirements (from discovery):
- Workloads: 60% live agent assist (streaming partial suggestions + final completion), 25% ticket summarization (post-call batch), 15% tool-calling (CRM update snippets).
- Latency: target p50 <40ms, p95 <90ms, p99 <=150ms for suggestion tokens end-to-end in US region. Must demonstrate performance under spikes (graceful degradation to cached prompts or smaller quantized variants).
- Throughput: expected steady-state 5k concurrent agent connections, burst up to 20k during peak campaigns.
- Quality: bullet-point summarization with 3-4 action items; hallucination minimization required for CRM updates. Guardrails: response validation & allow-listed actions for tool-calls.
- Model preferences: open models preferred; willing to evaluate Redwood-verified variants and quantized variants for cost. Need fallbacks: lower-cost model under heavy load, with transparent latency/cost routing.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and trace links required for each suggestion.
- Compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logging for all tool-calls, KMS integration for keys, EU data residency for subset of customers.

POC scope and acceptance criteria:
- Redwood to stand up a dedicated POC env (VPC peered) with streaming endpoint, provide perf runbook and test harness.
- Measure p99 latency under three load profiles: steady 5k, burst 12k, extreme 20k. Acceptance: p99 <=150ms in steady/burst; under extreme, system must fallback to a documented lower-tier model with no silent failures.
- Provide sample UI hooks (streaming deltas) and example validation logic for tool-calling (idempotency + allow-list).
- Security sign-off: complete SAML integration and pass basic audit checklist.

Quotes and paraphrase:
- "If suggestions lag, agents will ignore them — latency is non-negotiable." — Head of Product.
- "We like the routing ideas (cost vs latency) — need clarity on how rollbacks work." — VP Eng.
